document.title: feat(host-control): let Deck Apps call linked computers through built-in and custom plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control: linking, an SDK client, the Host Companion and a Shell screen, plus events, plugin packages, standalone plugins and agent skills.
document.why: A Deck App had no way to reach the computer next to it, as [PR #144](source:s1) states.

sources.label: chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #144
sources.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
sources.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unauthorized peers before reading their bodies**

When a non-linked LAN peer sends a slow or concurrent request, `reply` waits for `readBody` to finish before checking `isAllowed`; `readBody` continues consuming the stream and buffers up to 64 KiB per request, so denied peers can tie up sockets and memory before receiving a 403. Check the peer before reading the body, or abort unauthorized requests immediately, so the allowlist also protects availability.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

sources.body: Risk: high. This adds a boot-time LAN HTTP listener, persisted host links, plugin loading, and long-polling host events, so it is above the medium approval threshold and was not approved. Cursor Bugbot was skipped and no Security Agent check ran; human review is needed and no reviewers were assigned.

sources.label: fix(shell): an empty Shell focuses Host Control so Cross keeps listening

lookFor: [#109](source:s2) keeps `defineHostCommands` internal, with flat command names and a `HostCapabilities.commands` list. At head `defineHostPlugin` and `implementHostPlugin` are public, requests carry `plugin`, and capabilities list `plugins`. [PR #144](source:s1) names this deviation.

[#109](source:s2) has the client read `nativeGetHostControlUrl()`. At head it reads `nativeGetHostControlLinks()`, a JSON array of up to 4 links, and `createHostClient` takes a `hostId`. [PR #144](source:s1) says VitaDeck keeps several links.
[#109](source:s2) asks for a new `test:sdk` script in the `fast` tier. At head there is none: `test:cli` now also runs `test/host-control.test.ts`. No source gives a reason.
[#110](source:s3) targets Node 22+. At head the companion README and the `vitadeck-host-control` skill require Node.js 24. No source gives a reason.

[#110](source:s3) specifies the config `{ port, advertise, vita, enable }`. At head it is `{ id, name, port, advertise, vitas }`, with no `enable`. [PR #144](source:s1) relinks every Vita a companion linked and ships only read-only built-ins.

[#111](source:s4) has a link listener on 8798 that runs only while the Host Control screen is open. At head `POST /link` is a route on the LAN Listener, on from boot at 8787, and the harness checks it keeps running after a link. [PR #144](source:s1) says the first setup felt clunky.
[#111](source:s4) stores one link in `host-control-link.json`. At head `host-control-links.json` holds up to 4 links, newest first, one per companion `id`. [PR #144](source:s1) lists this deviation.

[#111](source:s4) says upload behaves exactly as before. At head upload runs from boot, and every accepted socket gets a 15 s per-read receive timeout (`VD_LAN_RECV_TIMEOUT_SEC`) that the old server did not set. No source mentions the timeout.

[PR #144](source:s1) records that Codex flagged the unpublished `@vitadeck/host-companion` devDependency in the #145 scaffold, declined as a release decision. At head both plugin templates still list it, and `copy-templates.ts` writes `^0.1.0`.
[Cursor's review](source:s8) rated the PR high risk and asked for human review. At head the LAN Listener starts at boot, and `/upload` and `/link` accept any LAN peer without credentials.

attention.note: `send` races the transport against a `setTimeout`, because the Vita `fetch` has no `AbortSignal`. A command that takes 6 s resolves `timeout` at 5 s, but the native request keeps running and the companion still runs it. Callers must read `timeout` as "may have run"; the client never retries.

groups.title: Events by long-polling
groups.why: No ticket asks for events; [PR #144](source:s1) adds them so plugins can push to Deck Apps.
groups.summary: Plugins emit events from a `start` lifecycle into the companion's event log, and `core.events` holds each request until the plugin's next event or 25 s. `watchHostEvents` in the SDK keeps one such request open per watcher.

attention.note: `wait` reads an `after` above the current `seq` as a restart and starts over from now. If a restarted companion emits 3 events before a wait with `after: 57`, the reply is `{ events: [], next: 3 }` and those 3 are lost. After 60 events it returns only 58 to 60. The ADR calls events best effort.

fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/events.ts: Keeps 100 events per plugin; `close` answers every waiting request.
fileNotes.js/packages/host-companion/src/core.ts: `events` answers `unknown_plugin` for an unloaded plugin; `notify` emits `notice`.
`watchHostEvents` retries a failed wait after 5 s, or 30 s on `timeout`.
fileNotes.js/packages/sdk/test/host-control.test.t: `next` becomes `after`; stopping from a callback ends at once.

groups.title: Fetch cancels on Deck App stop
groups.summary: `fetch_shutdown` marks every pending fetch cancelled and curl's progress callback aborts it, so a held event wait no longer stalls a Deck App stop.

attention.note: Stopping a Deck App now aborts every pending fetch, not only event waits. A Deck App's POST still in flight at a reload is cut off within about a second. Before, the stop waited for it, up to curl's 30 s cap.

fileNotes.tests/js_limits_harness.c: A server that never answers; stopping must take under 3 s.

groups.title: Companion installs and reloads packages
groups.why: [PR #145](source:s5) says a globally installed companion could not load a plugin installed elsewhere.
groups.summary: The companion loads `.vdplugin` packages from its `plugins/` folder and each `--plugin` path, and reloads them when their files change.

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): relink attempts run one at a time and re-read the config
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Retries for different Vitas ran on independent timers, and each save
wrote the same temporary file from a config read before the request.
All attempts now share one queue, a failure is logged, and linkVita
reads the config again just before changing its Vitas. Also list
unknown_link with the other link endpoint codes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A new computer IP or companion port broke commands until the user ran
`link` again. `start` now re-sends the link to every Vita in its config
with `relink: true`, which VitaDeck applies only to a link it still has,
so a computer forgotten in the Shell is not linked back: VitaDeck
answers 404 `unknown_link` and the companion drops that Vita. A Vita
that does not answer is retried every 30 s. The host-control demo asks
for capabilities again when a relink changes the URL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(shell): an install keeps Home focus on the entry row it was on
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Package rows sit above Upload and link and Host Control, and focus is a
row index, so the first upload into an empty library moved focus from
Host Control onto Upload and link, where the next Cross stopped the
listener.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
With no Deck App installed, Home opened on Upload and link, and the first
Cross stopped the listener the empty-state hint points to. Also shut down
client sockets while holding the listener lock, and fix two stale lines
in ADR 0004 and the upload script.

commits.subject: feat(shell): one LAN Listener for upload and link, on from startup
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Setting up a Deck App with a Host Control Plugin needed two Shell steps
and two addresses: start Upload for `vitadeck dev`, then open Host
Control for `link`. The upload server now also serves `POST /link`,
VitaDeck starts it at boot, and the Shell row turns it off and on. Both
CLIs take the same Vita address (port 8787).

commits.subject: feat(host-control): computers push events to Deck Apps by long-polling
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A plugin declares Host Control Events next to its commands and emits them
from a start(emit) lifecycle the companion runs while it is loaded. The
companion numbers recent events, and core.events holds a request until the
plugin's next event or 25 s. watchHostEvents in the SDK keeps one such
request open, so an event reaches the Vita within one round trip. core.notify
and `vitadeck-host-companion notify` let any script send a notice, which the
host-control demo shows.

Stopping a Deck App now cancels its pending fetches through curl's progress
callback, so a held request no longer stalls a reload or shutdown.

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.
